transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-06-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samuel Ortiz, Tasha Li (Redwood); Priya Raman, Liam O'Neill, Sara Khan, Devon Park, Anita Gomez (Acero)

--- Summary (auto):
Maya: quick recap, we looked at the dashboard, p95's are creeping up during the 12-2pm window, likely due to marketing bursts. Discussed increasing min replicas vs keeping low min and relying on burst capacity. Talked through KV cache warmup and prefix cache to improve cold starts. Agreed to sizing workbook update and synthetic benchmark.

--- Action items (auto):
- Maya to share sizing workbook with burst scenarios
- Liam to provide traffic samples and current autoscaler metrics
- Samuel to run quantized benchmark
- Devon to share security constraints

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription has occasional errors):
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh let's kick off. quick context for folks, this is our weekly POC sync to lock down Dedicated sizing and autoscale tuning for the pilot.
[00:00:12] Priya Raman: thanks Maya, hi team. we've got Liam and Devon on from infra and security, sara from product. we want to make sure the system doesn't blow up during our campaign next month  last time we saw tail p99s spike.
[00:00:28] Samuel Ortiz: yeah so last week's run, the dashboard shows average qps ~120 but we saw 800 qps bursts for 2-3 minutes around noon. p95 was stable at ~180ms but p99 jumped to 1.1s during the burst window.
[00:00:45] Liam O'Neill: and to add we have autoscaler set to min 2 max 12 right now, cooldown 180s, but the ramp-up is slow because of cold-starts and kv cash warmups, chip in devon 
[00:01:01] Devon Park: yeah sorry kv cash  cache, the prefix cache isn't fully warmed since sessions are short lived from mobile. we also have strict VPC peering and egress rules which makes some of the node prefetch slower.
[00:01:18] Maya Chen: got it, thanks. two levers: bump steady-state min to reduce cold-starts or keep low min and rely on burst capacity. both have cost/latency tradeoffs. Samuel, can you remind what we saw when we increased min from 2 to 5 in the dry run?
[00:01:34] Samuel Ortiz: sure, when min=5 the p99 during bursts dropped from 1.1s to ~420ms, cost increased about ~26% in that simulated 24h run. With min=2 + burst reserves (pre-launched spare nodes) we saw p99 ~550ms but cost delta ~12% with reserved burst nodes only active during market windows.
[00:01:58] Sara Khan: what's the operational complexity of burst reserves vs autoscaler? we don't want to own a bunch of manual runbooks.
[00:02:07] Tasha Li: Redwood supports policy-based burst: you can configure scheduled scale-up windows, traffic-threshold triggers, and soft-reservations that keep a hot pool in a different capacity tier. We'll put recommended defaults in the workbook.
[00:02:22] Priya Raman: how quick are the cold-starts with the larger models? our prompts are often long (1k tokens).
[00:02:30] Samuel Ortiz: cold-starts depend on KV cache and model weight loading. With the quantized int8 path we saw weight load times down ~35%, and streaming generation had similar per-token latency, so cold-start fell from ~850ms to ~520ms in our bench. but the KV cache warmup for repeated prefixes still matters  we can do prefix caching for common templates.
[00:02:53] Liam O'Neill: and remember network egress to the KMS for key unwrap adds ~40-60ms on cold init, that's on top. our security team is checking if we can keep a local key cache or use a regional HSM to cut that.
[00:03:10] Devon Park: yes we'll check with the KMS folks. also a note, SSO provisioning needs to be active before dedicated console access.
[00:03:18] Maya Chen: noted. ok on burst scenarios: we generally model two types  short high QPS spikes (2-5 mins) and mid-length campaigns (30-90 mins). Which one is more critical for you?
[00:03:29] Priya Raman: both, but the short spikes are the worst for user-visible latency; the 30-90 minute ones are fine if we have steady capacity.
[00:03:37] Samuel Ortiz: so recommendation: keep min replicas modest (3-5) for baseline and add a burst policy that pre-warms X nodes when threshold hit and also scheduled pre-scale 5 mins before known campaigns. That reduces p99 for the short spike without 24/7 cost of higher min.
[00:03:53] Anita Gomez: curious about quantization risk to output quality  our QA worried that int8 will hallucinate more.
[00:04:02] Samuel Ortiz: fair  our internal evals show minimal delta at 8-bit for instruction-following tasks; we'll run a quality regression on your eval set during the synthetic benchmark and share diff metrics. if we see regressions we'll fallback to a 4-bit nf4 profile or mixed precision for sensitive routes.
[00:04:21] Sara Khan: can we route high-sensitivity requests to hosted fallback to avoid any risk?
[00:04:26] Maya Chen: yes that's a common pattern  route PII/sensitive to hosted or to a pinned high-precision model. Redwood routing policies can do per-route fallbacks automatically.
[00:04:36] Priya Raman: good. on the sizing workbook, can you include cost deltas between strategies? we need to show finance.
[00:04:42] Maya Chen: absolutely. the workbook will include: steady-state min options, burst pool size, scheduled scaling windows, and per-strategy 30-day cost projection.
[00:04:52] Liam O'Neill: one more infra constraint: we can't allow nodes to spin up in a different VPC without peering; peering takes ops time. so any burst plan needs either pre-peered capacity or allow some buffer for peering setup.
[00:05:05] Tasha Li: we'll add notes about network pre-reqs and a recommended runbook for peering and routing fallback.
[00:05:12] Devon Park: security wise, we'll need the SOC2 questionnaire filled and the KMS key policy doc. Maya can you drop the security pack link?
[00:05:20] Maya Chen: yes i'll share the security pack and SOC2 artifacts in the follow-up.
[00:05:25] [00:05:28] Samuel Ortiz: quick question on metrics  can you provide the tail latency SLOs and target cost per 1M tokens? That helps pick quantization vs hardware.
[00:05:36] Priya Raman: p95 target 250ms, p99 <600ms for interactive flows; cost target TBD but ideally less than our current vendor by 20%.
[00:05:47] Samuel Ortiz: got it. we'll model those in the workbook.
[00:05:50] [00:06:00] (discussion continues, details of workbook columns and synthetic bench plan)
[00:06:05] Samuel Ortiz: plan for bench: we run int8 and nf4 variants across 8,16,24 token windows with 1k prompt seeds from Acero's sample corpus. we'll measure p50/p95/p99, cold-starts, and token/sec.
[00:06:20] Anita Gomez: for sample corpus i'll redact PHI and send a dev-only subset.
[00:06:26] Priya Raman: yes we'll sanitize before sending.
[00:06:30] Maya Chen: perfect. timeline check  we aim to have sizing workbook and synthetic logs by end of next week. any blockers?
[00:06:37] Liam O'Neill: just internal approvals for traffic export; should be ok by Friday.
[00:06:42] Devon Park: security has a few SOC questions but nothing blocking the bench.
[00:06:46] Maya Chen: great. last thing  status of dedicated capacity commitment? finance asked for a 3 month min commit for discounted burst pricing, is that something you can consider?
[00:06:58] Priya Raman: we'll discuss with finance but likely yes if the numbers look good. please include committed vs payg cost in the workbook.
[00:07:07] Maya Chen: will do. ok let's wrap with next steps.
[00:07:11] (recap)
[00:07:12] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood updates sizing workbook w/ burst scenarios and committed vs payg columns (Maya). Acero shares 7-day trace and sanitized sample corpus (Liam/Anita). Samuel runs synthetic bench and shares results (Samuel). Devon shares KMS/SSO constraints and SOC2 questions (Devon). We'll reconvene same time next week.
[00:07:36] Priya Raman: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[00:07:39] Maya Chen: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
